title: I Love Thy Church, O God
description: I Love Thy Church, O God in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Timothy Dwight wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 657 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Attachment to the Church”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I love thy church, O God; Her walls be-fore thee stand, Dear as the ap-ple of thine eye, And gra-ven on thy hand.

lines: I love thy church, O God;
Dear as the apple of thine eye,
For her my tears shall fall;
To her my cares and toils be given,
Till toils and cares shall end.
Her hymns of love and praise.
Thy hand, from every snare and foe,
Sure as thy truth shall last,
The brightest glories earth can yield,

licence: Public domain: Timothy Dwight died in 1817.
credits: Words by Timothy Dwight (1752–1817), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
